themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models begin by logging thousands of real buyer questions and still say the output is non-deterministic with no stable baseline; the same gap drives cross-channel incrementality, identity resolution, B2B buying-group signal loss, and content review, where reviewers themselves disagree.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people who hold the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can make them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers offer fast lanes and better prices so declaring beats spoofing, journey orchestration answers admit channel owners are paid to keep sending, semantic layer answers call conflicting definitions a political settlement, and ad supply answers say the open web profits from fake volume.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Consent and deletion answers describe ad platforms and agency segments as black boxes and say a person cannot be pulled back out of a trained model; incrementality answers note platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and ad supply answers distrust vendor-reported impressions.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every agent execution answer puts a proxy or gateway in front of martech writes with spend and audience caps because sends and spend cannot be rolled back; consent answers funnel all data exits through a single checkpoint and journey orchestration answers add one shared pre-send check.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Content governance answers all converge on approved-claim libraries that constrain what can be said because implied meaning cannot be checked automatically, and semantic layer answers argue a single definition of customer is the wrong target when teams legitimately need different ones.
